# Ari Harrison

> Founder, NovoMCP. Building the open computational chemistry engine for drug discovery and materials science.

## Now

- Building: NovoMCP - the open computational chemistry engine. MCP + REST, 69 tools, self-hostable under Apache-2.0 or set up by NovoMCP on your infrastructure under a branded subdomain. Clone it and it boots with zero external services - no auth, no account, no API key. Shipped through v1.4.3 (ALCHEMI-accelerated axis across geometry/energy/conformers; in-process cheminformatics sourced from the open novomcp-lite package). Solo founder.
- Shipped: Novo Station - the NovoMCP compute core on NVIDIA DGX Spark (GPU molecular dynamics, GPU docking, MACE / ANI-2x potentials, ALCHEMI, xTB / CREST, 31 ADMET models) on one GB10 desktop system from one compose file. Measured at about 0.4x a datacenter L40S's raw MD speed and 1.2-1.5x its throughput per watt (GROMACS water benchmark, 2026). Structure prediction, generative design, and free-energy methods are outside this release. https://novomcp.com/novo-station
- Open source: novomcp-lite - a lightweight, standalone version of NovoMCP's cheminformatics (for when you just want the wrappers, not the whole engine), Apache-2.0, on PyPI (pip install novomcp-lite). Eight zero-config tools (RDKit properties/profiling/synthetic-accessibility/PAINS-BRENK alerts/library screening + ChEMBL/ClinicalTrials.gov/bioRxiv search) as a Python library or MCP server; same code as the full engine, so the numbers match - just without the rest of the engine. https://github.com/NovoMCP/novomcp-lite
- Open source: the engine's GPU compute services ship as standalone Apache-2.0 repos, each deployable on its own - gromacs-md (GROMACS MD, https://github.com/NovoMCP/gromacs-md), novomcp-nnp (neural-network potentials, https://github.com/NovoMCP/novomcp-nnp), novomcp-qm (quantum chemistry, https://github.com/NovoMCP/novomcp-qm).
- Open source: NovoMD - local-first molecular descriptor library, MIT-licensed, ships as a Python library + CLI + Hugging Face MCP endpoint + Docker REST. https://github.com/ariharrisonlab/NovoMD
- Open to: Product Manager and 0-to-1 product leadership roles. Bay Area or remote. Particularly interested in production AI systems, MCP-shaped infrastructure, and applied AI at companies where correctness matters.
- Contact: ariharrisonlab@gmail.com / LinkedIn (linkedin.com/in/ariharrisonlab).

## About

The interesting problem isn't getting a model to say something. It's building the system around the model so its output can be acted on - safely, correctly, repeatedly, with a record of what happened. That's the work.

NovoMCP is what I built. One computational chemistry engine, 69 in-silico tools across ADMET, docking, molecular dynamics, quantum chemistry, structure prediction, and compliance, that speaks both MCP (reachable from Claude Desktop, Cursor, Codex, Zed, and any MCP-compatible assistant) and REST (any pipeline that posts JSON). It wraps established open compute (RDKit, GROMACS, AutoDock-GPU, OpenFold, Boltz, Gnina, xTB, ANI-2x, AIMNet2, MACE) rather than reimplementing it. Two paths to run it: self-host it under Apache-2.0 on your own hardware - it boots with zero external services, no auth, no account, no API key - or have NovoMCP set it up on your infrastructure under a branded subdomain, with the hosted FAVES compliance API and FEP alongside. Same engine either way; a pluggable auth/metering/audit spine (NOVO_AUTH / NOVO_METER / NOVO_AUDIT = local / hosted / custom) swaps the two with no code fork.

The engine, never the platform (positioning call). Scale-to-zero by default (unit economics call). Human-in-the-loop via MCP elicitation, not autonomous-agent-on-someone-else's-molecules (trust call). Open-sourced as an engine, not as a hosted product (moat call - the moat is FAVES compliance + FEP + the deployment service, not the code).

Before NovoMCP: reinforcement learning agents for autonomous discovery in high-stakes manufacturing. The systems ran continuously, diagnosed their own failures, and improved without intervention. Different domain, same problem shape - the agent isn't the product; the system that makes the agent safe to deploy is the product. That's the throughline.

## The Stack

- The Engine: MCP + REST, 69 tools, 18 always-available on a fresh clone (now v1.4.3)
- Desktop GPU: Novo Station, the compute core on NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10), one compose file
- Runs local: boots with zero external services - no auth, no account, no API key; audit to ~/.novo/audit.jsonl
- Pluggable spine: auth / metering / audit swap local <-> hosted <-> custom by env flag - same code standalone or operated
- Wraps open compute: RDKit, GROMACS, AutoDock-GPU, OpenFold, Boltz, Gnina, xTB, ANI-2x, AIMNet2, MACE; ALCHEMI-accelerated engine axis across geometry, energy, and conformer search (through v1.3.0); in-process cheminformatics sourced from the open novomcp-lite package (v1.4.0)
- License: Apache-2.0 (orchestration core BSL 1.1 -> Apache 2029-07-12)
- Compliance: FAVES V4 (hosted API) - 8 regulatory frameworks, 1,585 structural alerts
- Surfaces: MCP + REST + Workbench (v1.5.x) + Chrome ext + Word add-in + bundled dashboard
- Verticals: Drug discovery + materials science
- Ecosystem: NVIDIA Inception, AWS Activate, Microsoft Founders Hub

## Publications

Research on how domain structure shapes reasoning - and how reasoning systems adapt under different objective and constraint regimes.

- FAVES V4: A Production-Deployed Compliance and Liability Screening System for Drug Discovery at 122M-Compound Scale (2026.05, ChemRxiv) - Production compliance and liability screening aligned to HHS/ONC FAVES and NIST AI 600-1. Single-API call returns regulatory status (DEA / FDA / CWC / EPA / EU REACH), 1,585 structural alerts, BOILED-Egg permeability, and InChIKey prior-art lookup. Scored 341 of 342 across five predetermined tests; the one miss was a whitelist bug (a wrong SMILES for cortisol) that the full benchmark caught and change control fixed. Documented governance bundle. About 0.45 s per call with a cached prior-art answer, about 3.1 s with a live PubChem lookup (May 2026 benchmark). DOI: 10.26434/chemrxiv.15003738/v3

- NovoExpert-2: ADMET Prediction via Gradient-Boosted Trees on MapLight Fingerprints and GIN Embeddings (2026.04, ChemRxiv) - Three audited wins over the current TDC #1 (MapLight+GNN) on AUPRC, TDC's standard metric for these endpoints: CYP3A4 Substrate, Carbon-Mangels (+0.013); Clearance Hepatocyte, AZ (+0.011); DILI (+0.003 to +0.006). None clears the +0.02 landmark margin. CatBoost ensembles with MapLight and GIN fingerprints, plus Chemprop v2 D-MPNN for DILI. DOI: 10.26434/chemrxiv.15000061/v2

## Projects

- NovoMCP - the open computational chemistry engine (https://github.com/NovoMCP/novomcp): One engine, two surfaces (MCP + REST). 69 tools across cheminformatics, ADMET, docking, MD, quantum chemistry, structure prediction, materials science, and an 11-stage autonomous discovery funnel. Clone it and it boots with zero external services - no auth, no account, no API key; 18 tools work with a fresh clone, the rest unlock as you wire optional compute. A pluggable spine (auth / metering / audit) swaps local <-> hosted <-> custom by env flag - no OSS/enterprise fork. Wraps open compute (RDKit, GROMACS, AutoDock-GPU, OpenFold, Boltz, Gnina, xTB, ANI-2x, MACE) with an ALCHEMI-accelerated axis across geometry, energy, and conformer search (through v1.3.0), and sources its in-process cheminformatics from the open novomcp-lite package (v1.4.0). Apache-2.0 top-level; orchestration core BSL 1.1 -> Apache 2029-07-12. Works with Claude Desktop, Cursor, Codex, Zed, ChatGPT, Gemini, and any MCP-compatible assistant, or hit it from your own code over HTTP. https://novomcp.com/engine

- Novo Station - the NovoMCP compute core on NVIDIA DGX Spark (https://novomcp.com/novo-station): GROMACS GPU MD, AutoDock-GPU docking, MACE and ANI-2x potentials, the ALCHEMI toolkit, xTB / CREST, and 31 ADMET models on one GB10 desktop system, from one compose file of prebuilt arm64 images. Measured against a datacenter L40S: about 0.4x the raw MD speed at about a third of the power, so 1.2-1.5x the throughput per watt. Outside this release: structure prediction, generative design, free-energy methods. Three default tools still query public databases (ChEMBL, RCSB, bioRxiv). Quickstart: https://docs.novomcp.com/novo-station-dgx-spark/. Field report on the five porting failures: https://www.novomcp.com/news/what-actually-breaks-when-you-port-a-chemistry-stack-to-dgx-spark. The reproducible workload is submitted to NVIDIA's DGX Spark playbooks.

- novomcp-lite - NovoMCP's cheminformatics as a lightweight standalone package (https://github.com/NovoMCP/novomcp-lite): the lite version, for when you just want the wrappers rather than the full engine. Apache-2.0, two dependencies, on PyPI (pip install novomcp-lite). Eight zero-config tools - RDKit properties, profiling, synthetic-accessibility, PAINS/BRENK structural alerts, library screening, plus public-API search (ChEMBL, ClinicalTrials.gov, bioRxiv) - as a Python library or an MCP server. Same code the full engine runs on, so the numbers match - just without the rest of the engine. Prompted by user feedback (a researcher who wired the engine up to his agent and asked for a lighter, wrappers-only build).

- FAVES compliance API: The moat around the OSS engine. Compliance and liability screening for pharma / biotech pipelines - regulatory status across eight frameworks (DEA, FDA, EPA, EU REACH, Australian schedule, CWC, BTWC, OPCW), 1,585 structural alerts, BOILED-Egg pharmacokinetics, and prior-art lookup, with per-field provenance and a PROCEED / STOP / CAUTION verdict. Validated with predetermined acceptance criteria (341/342 recorded), seven governance documents, an audit trail on every call. Informational early-discovery screening, not a regulatory determination. Closed and paid; access on request. Not shipped with the OSS engine. https://novomcp.com/faves

- NovoWorkbench - native desktop for the engine (design-partner preview): The molecule canvas, 3D viewers, and discovery funnel as a native desktop for macOS and Windows. Local RDKit, offline alert screening (PAINS + druglikeness rule sets), bring-your-own-LLM chat, model-agnostic. Tauri + Python sidecar; Apple Developer ID notarized (team 8N9K9B7Y69). Currently in design-partner preview; ships as OSS in v1.5.x per the product roadmap. https://novomcp.com/novoworkbench

- Chrome extension (browser surface): Hover any SMILES on PubChem, ChEMBL, DrugBank, or preprints for instant ADMET, compliance, similarity search. Side panel for advanced compute. "Continue in AI" deep-links into MCP-connected assistants. Manifest V3, whitelisted hosts only. Ships as a sideload (load unpacked, point it at your own engine): https://github.com/NovoMCP/novomcp-chrome-sideload

- Word add-in (editor surface, private beta): Inline SMILES profiling and compliance tables in Word documents - manuscripts, protocols, grants. Office.js add-in, static-hosted manifest at addin.novomcp.com. Repo: https://github.com/NovoMCP/novomcp-word-sideload

- REST API (developer surface): Single endpoint shape - POST /mcp/tools/{name}. Ships in the open engine (localhost:8018); the tool catalog is the OpenAPI 3.1 spec generated from the tool registry. Same backend as MCP, zero code duplication. It ran first as a hosted, metered gateway at api.novomcp.com; hosted billing was retired with the open-source release, and api.novomcp.com now hosts the two closed services: the FAVES compliance API and FEP. https://novomcp.com/api

- Bundled dashboard (control room): A minimal Next.js dashboard that ships bundled with the open engine at frontend-nextjs/ in the OSS repo. Runs on localhost when self-hosted; on the branded subdomain when NovoMCP sets it up. Minimal today, growing with each release. https://github.com/NovoMCP/novomcp/tree/main/frontend-nextjs

- NovoMD (open source, MIT, https://github.com/ariharrisonlab/NovoMD): Local-first molecular descriptor library. SMILES in, 32+ descriptors out from a 3D conformer (geometry, energy, electrostatics, surface, volume), calculated on the user's own machine with no account and no API key. Four runtimes from one core: pip-installable Python library, CLI with batch/explain/report subcommands, a hosted Hugging Face MCP endpoint (quantnexusai-novomd.hf.space) that works with Claude / Cursor / Continue / any MCP client, and a Docker REST service. Deliberately scoped: no ADMET, no pKa, no binding affinity, no solubility predictions - that boundary is documented in the README and shipped as an agent skill telling AI assistants explicitly where the tool's authority ends. Determinism guarantee: same SMILES, identical descriptors, any machine.

- Product portfolio (https://ariharrisonlab.github.io/portfolio.html): Each surface as a product case - problem, decision, build, outcome. Plus cross-cutting decisions: engine-first language, scale-to-zero by default, Azure to AWS migration, private-endpoint infra, opening the engine at v1.0, and human-in-the-loop over autonomy.

## Leadership decisions

Selected product, infra, and positioning calls made shipping NovoMCP. Posted in full at https://ariharrisonlab.github.io/#leadership.

- Open the engine at v1.0: Apache-2.0 top-level, BSL 1.1 -> Apache 2029-07-12 for the orchestration core. The moat is FAVES compliance + FEP + the deployment service, not the code that calls RDKit and orchestrates docking, and not the models (their weights are open on Hugging Face, https://huggingface.co/NovoMCP). Distribution flips from "sign up for our platform" to "clone the repo."
- Scale-to-zero by default: every compute service ships with min_replicas=0; only public-path surfaces stay warm. Unit economics stay honest day one.
- "Engine" never "platform": locked public language to "computational chemistry engine"; positioning rule rather than positioning deck.
- Killed the campaign / autonomous-run system. Replaced with human-in-the-loop via MCP elicitation at every funnel stage. The audit log is the quality gate.
- Self-hosted or set up for you, no middle: killed the prior Free Trial / Core / Scale / Enterprise credit-tier ladder at the OSS launch. Two paths: self-hosted (free forever, Apache-2.0) or a deployment service (contact for pricing; NovoMCP sets the engine up on your infrastructure under a branded subdomain). No self-serve middle tier.
- Private-endpoint-only infra (EKS API, Aurora, Redis, internal ALBs). Build on GH-hosted runners, deploy via OIDC -> SSM -> bastion. Pattern applied uniformly across every service.
